action_semantics._note: candidate.action and live_issue.disposition are DIFFERENT axes and must not be cross-read. A candidate action describes what happens to a unit of canonical work; a disposition describes what happens to an existing GitHub issue number.

candidate.action.KEEP: Canonical work already correctly represented; no edit needed.
candidate.action.UPDATE: One live issue carries this work and is corrected in place, preserving its number.
candidate.action.SPLIT: This candidate is one of several produced from a single live issue whose canonical boundary changed. Exactly one sibling inherits the original issue number (role=primary); the others are created new in Phase 3.
candidate.action.MERGE: This candidate absorbs scope from TWO OR MORE live issues. Exactly one contributor is role=primary and keeps its issue number; the others contribute scope only. A contributor's own issue-level disposition is INDEPENDENT of this action.
candidate.action.CREATE: No live issue exists; a new issue is opened in Phase 3. live_issues is empty.
candidate.action.CLOSE_SUPERSEDED: Not used as a candidate action in this matrix; closure is an issue-level disposition only.

live_issue.disposition.UPDATE: Issue is corrected in place and keeps its number.
live_issue.disposition.SPLIT: Issue's scope divides across several candidates; it keeps its number for the candidate where it is role=primary and is narrowed accordingly.
live_issue.disposition.MERGE: Issue is WHOLLY absorbed into a candidate primarily carried by a different issue. It retains no independent scope and is closed in Phase 3 with a pointer to the absorbing issue. Not used in this matrix — see _merge_note.
live_issue.disposition.CLOSE_SUPERSEDED: Issue is closed. closure_kind distinguishes `superseded` (successors exist, named in superseded_by) from `canonically_removed` (the canon deleted the work and nothing replaces it).

action_semantics._merge_note: This matrix contains one MERGE candidate (M0-I1) and zero MERGE dispositions. That is correct, not an inconsistency. M0-I1 absorbs the full-stack composition scope from Backend#4 into Infrastructure#1. Infrastructure#1 is role=primary and keeps its number (disposition UPDATE). Backend#4 is NOT wholly absorbed — it retains the Backend service Dockerfile as M0-B4 — so its disposition is SPLIT, not MERGE. A MERGE disposition would only apply to an issue left with no independent scope at all.
action_semantics._phase3_rule: Phase 3 MUST derive 'which issue number is edited' from live_issues[].role == 'primary', never from candidate.action. A MERGE or SPLIT action never by itself implies closing an issue; only an issue-level disposition of MERGE or CLOSE_SUPERSEDED does.

candidates.proposed_title: Establish a representative performance and query baseline with evidence-based indexing
detected_drift: 'GET /households/{id}/tasks with 1000 tasks returns <200ms' is an unqualified gate with no percentile, environment, dataset definition or duration.
